layers.author: V. V. S. Aiyar
layers.work_title: The Kural, or The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar
layers.rights_evidence: Public domain by date. The scan's title page (PDF p3): 'THE KURAL OR The Maxims of Tiruvalluvar, TRANSLATED BY V. V. S. AIYAR ... PUBLISHED BY SUBRAHMANYA SHIVA, 8 Pichu Pillai Street, Mylapore, Madras S., 1916'; p2: 'Books can be had of the Author V. V. S. Aiyar, 89 Dharmaraja Covil Street, Pondichery'. Published 1916; translator d. 3 June 1925. No copyright notice appears on the front or back pages of the scan. Scope: Aiyar's verse translations only (PDF pp. 59-328). Not in the layer: his Preface (signed V.V.S. AIYAR), his Notes and the advertisement pages, chapter headings, speaker labels, footnote marks, and the two epigraphs on the title page quoted from M. Ariel and Gover; no foreword or editorial matter by another hand was found in the OCR of the front matter. Secondary statement, not a primary source: public domain in India (60 years after the author's death) and in the United States; Standard Ebooks editorial markup dedicated CC0. The Commons file page's Public-domain / PD-US template (unverified) and the PDF's RC4 owner flag (copy:no, print:no, empty user password) are properties of the file, not copyright facts; scan source Digital Library of India 2015.203867 via Internet Archive in.ernet.dli.2015.203867. No legal ruling: flagged. Kurals 6-10 and 36-40 are not in the scan (PDF p60 repeats p59, p66 is blank): they come from the Standard Ebooks epub (typed edition, 2024-04-15, from English Wikisource and Internet Archive in.ernet.dli.2015.102804), source se:aiyar-kural, tier typed_edition_only. Its imprint: 'The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain ... They may still be copyrighted in other countries ... The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication.' The text is machine-read from the scan, not a transcription: five machine readings by two engines (each engine on the full-resolution page, both on a half-resolution copy, and the second engine on a 1.5x copy; the resampled readings repeat an engine on the same pixels, a weaker independence), then compared with the Standard Ebooks typing as a second witness (it modernises some spellings and has its own slips, so it settles a word only by a logged rule or by a ruling made from the page image). The tier of every row (ocr_letters_punct_agree, ocr_letters_agree, ocr_auto_resolved, ocr_rule_resolved, ocr_se_resolved, adjudicated, typed_edition_only) is in its `tier` column and in provenance/reports/aiyar1916_page_check.json. No row is verified from the scan. Measured error rate (verse level, against the page images): on a 40-verse sample, 1 error: 0 of 24 in the agreeing tiers (95% upper limit 13.8%, a bound, not a claim of clean text) and 1 of 16 in ocr_rule_resolved. The sample predates rules R27-R37, which are not measured on held-out rows. Compared with the Standard Ebooks typing, 69 of 1,320 scan rows differed in a word before the typed-edition rules; the epub is itself fallible, so this is an upper bound on the reading error, not a rate.

layers.author: Parimelazhagar
layers.work_title: Commentary labelled Parimelazhagar in the Selvakumar dataset (column header 'Parimezhalagar_Urai'); upstream and printed edition not identified
layers.rights_evidence: Column header says Parimelazhagar; who typed it and from which edition is not stated (carrier README.md line 2 'license: mit'). Spot-check 2026-10-17 (provenance/reports/parimel_check.json): on 20 kurals the column shares a median 68% of its Tamil 5-grams with the Lazarus 1885 Parimelazhagar pages and 57% with the Navalar pages, against 30% / 18% for the modern Mu.Va meaning; consistent with the classical commentary, not a modern paraphrase. Author rights: public domain (Parimelazhagar's text). Transcription rights: unverified (typist and edition unknown). Kept out of the CC0 core; shipped under its carrier's MIT terms. The column has 11 virama-after-vowel sequences and digits (text_flags).
